brief: 5 SaaS categories AI agents are killing in 2026 — and what to build instead.

slots.title: 1. CRM, the dying database
slots.body: Static contact lists are dead. Build an AI relationship agent that updates itself, schedules follow-ups, and drafts context-aware emails without manual entry.

slots.title: 2. Task boards, the stale tracker
slots.body: Kanban cards don't execute code. Ship an agentic project layer that assigns tasks, predicts blockers, and autonomously resolves dependencies across teams.

slots.title: 3. Chatbots, the scripted gatekeeper
slots.body: FAQ trees frustrate users. Replace them with autonomous support engineers that debug issues, trigger refunds, and rewrite docs using live product context.

slots.title: 4. Dashboards, the passive report
slots.body: Charts don't close deals. Sell narrative intelligence agents that query metrics, draft board summaries, and recommend pricing changes in plain English.

slots.title: 5. Expense tools, the manual inbox
slots.body: Receipt chasing wastes hours. Launch finance agents that audit subscriptions, negotiate vendor bills, and forecast burn from unstructured Slack threads.

slots.title: 6. Infrastructure, the real moat
slots.body: Don't rebuild another SaaS UI. Build the memory layer, agent router, and trust framework that lets every company spawn its own vertical AI workforce.

slots.headline: Build the agent layer.
slots.subline: SaaS is becoming invisible. The winners in 2026 sell outcomes, not seats.
